sugestoes.texto: WHAT: readSequence loops while(length>0) with length-=bytes.length and never validates exact consumption or indefinite length -1. WHY: Overlong inner TLVs drive length negative and exit silently, and 0x80 indefinite length returns empty list, producing wrong R/S split or confusing downstream size error instead of rejecting malformed DER.

WHAT: integerToBytes silently truncates oversized integers to low qLength bytes and does not reject negative BigIntegers. WHY: Invalid DER R/S values are mapped to a different valid concatenated value instead of throwing, causing wrong output and signature malleability versus strict DER validation.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

Calling CryptoIntegration.init from AuthzClient.create is claimed to lock the global crypto provider to the minimal AuthzClientCryptoProvider so a later server init is ignored and unsupported operations fail.
The ignored-providers message is passed to logger.debugf as a format string instead of using logger.debug, and keeps a trailing comma.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: emailValidation depends on 'rejectedEmails.@each' for an array of primitive strings. WHY: @each observes properties of array items, not membership; pushObject(result.values.email) does not invalidate the computed property so the remembered rejected email error is not shown until accountEmail itself changes. HOW: Change dependent key to 'rejectedEmails.[]' (or 'rejectedEmails.length').

WHAT: EmailValidator.validate_each only checks whitelist/blacklist/blocked and never validates email syntax, while User now relies solely on validates :email, email:true for email shape. WHY: Malformed strings with no @/domain pass validation and create users with undeliverable emails, breaking mail delivery and downstream assumptions. HOW: Restore a format check (e.g. against User::EMAIL) in EmailValidator before the restriction/blocked checks.

issues.descricao: Claims the rejected-email memory stores the server-normalised email, so it never matches the raw input on retry.
Claims the 'rejectedEmails.@each' dependent key does not observe pushes of plain strings, so the rejection is not shown until the email changes.
BlockedEmail.should_block? returns nil instead of false when the email has no record.
Claims EmailValidator dropped the email format check that the old User#email_validator performed, allowing invalid emails.
Claims EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting? raises NoMethodError when the email is nil.
Claims the blocked-email validator specs would still pass if the blocked-email branch were removed.

`rejectedEmails` is declared as an array literal on the controller prototype, so it is shared across instances and modal sessions; emails rejected once keep failing validation later. Initialize it per instance in `init`.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: canView(user)/canManage(user) dropped AdminRoles.ADMIN from the fast-path role check present before. WHY: A master-realm ADMIN without MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS in the target realm now falls through to hasPermission which returns false when !isAdminSameRealm, denying legitimate master admins (regression). HOW: Restore ADMIN to the hasOneAdminRole checks.

issues.descricao: Claims removing the canView filter from searchForUser lets admins see users they are not allowed to view.
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission scans group resources and evaluates permissions for each on every user search or count request.
Claims deleting a group under V2 triggers the removal listener, which calls GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims testManageGroupMembership never exercises the group-level manage-membership permission.
searchForUser no longer filters results with usersEvaluator::canView, so an admin with query access but no view permission and no group grants gets an unrestricted user list.

GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) does not fall back to canView(), and the PR dropped the canViewGlobal short-circuit, so an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission is denied (and the group filtered out of listings) for any group that has its own permission resource lacking VIEW.
Claims GroupResource management-permissions endpoints call GroupPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, causing 500s when V2 is active.

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission does not restrict evaluated permissions to the evaluated resource, so when falling back to the all-groups resource a permission granted on one specific group can satisfy the check for any group.

GroupsResource.getGroups no longer hoists the global canView() check, so in FGAP V2 each listed group triggers its own resource lookup and policy evaluation even when an all-groups grant would cover them all.
UserPermissionsV2 canView/canManage dropped AdminRoles.ADMIN from the role check, claimed to deny admins view/manage access unlike V1.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: New offset code calls .tz(override.timeZone) and .tz(timeZone) without guarding optional/unknown zones and parses via override.start.toString(). WHY: Undefined/invalid zone from optional TimeRange.timeZone or invitee input throws or yields NaN offset, crashing slot generation or shifting all override times. HOW: Guard missing zones and parse Date directly with dayjs(override.start).tz().

WHAT: Per-day per-override path builds 6+ Dayjs+tz objects (two utcOffset lookups plus hour/minute extraction via repeated utc().add(offset)). WHY: Executed inside getTimeSlots day loop so cost scales O(days*overrides) with heavy date parsing on hot availability path. HOW: Parse each override once per call and reuse start/end minutes.

WHAT: Date-override shift uses dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 then add(utcOffset), inverting the UTC-to-wall conversion (wall = UTC + offset, not UTC - offset). WHY: Day matching and start/end range checks are shifted by twice the organizer offset in the wrong direction, so slots match the wrong override day and in/out-of-override verdicts are wrong for non-UTC organizers. HOW: Remove the * -1 (add the raw utcOffset) to match the offset-difference convention used in packages/lib/slots.ts.

issues.descricao: Claims checkIfIsAvailable interprets date overrides in organizerTimeZone instead of each override owner's timezone.
The new different-timezone date-override test expects the same UTC slots as the existing case and would still pass if the offset fix in slots.ts were reverted.
Claims the selected-slots availability call site passes only the user's timezone, so dateOverrides and workingHours fall back to [] and slots are checked only against busy times.
Claims getSlots uses the optional override.timeZone, so an override without it passes undefined to dayjs.tz and computes a wrong offset using the server timezone.
checkIfIsAvailable calls dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone) guarded only by truthiness, so an invalid time-zone string would throw and abort getSchedule.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getCalendarCredentials stays sync but `getCalendar(credential)` on line 28 now returns Promise<Calendar|null>, so `calendar` field stores a Promise instead of Calendar. WHY: Breaks the function's contract — callers found via grep (viewer.tsx:340,415, availability/calendar.ts:83) expecting Calendar get a Promise; only getConnectedCalendars was patched to `await item.calendar`, other uses of `.calendar` will call calendar methods on a Promise and crash/misbehave. HOW: Make getCalendarCredentials async and `await getCalendar(credential)` (or Promise.all), and update all 3 callers to await it.

WHAT: `getVideoAdapters` awaits each dynamic `import()` sequentially in `for (const cred of withCredentials) { await appStore[...] }`. WHY: N credentials cause N serial import resolutions instead of parallel, adding linear latency to every availability/meeting call (same pattern in handleCancelBooking.ts:480-482 for..of with await getCalendar). HOW: Resolve in parallel with `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))`.

issues.descricao: Suggests wrapping the awaited dynamic app import in try-catch to handle import failures, without identifying a defect.
Claims consumers of getCalendarCredentials call methods on or null-check an un-awaited Promise; every consumer goes through getConnectedCalendars, which awaits it.
Claims the import() calls in the appStore object load every app eagerly and should be thunks; the asynchronous loading works as intended.
The commented example entry in app-store/index.ts points to ./example instead of ./_example.
Claims getVideoAdapters performs N sequential module-load round trips per request; the imports already started in parallel at module load.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Check returns Allowed:true directly from stale permCache without DB revalidation. WHY: A permission revoked after the cache entry was written still authorizes for up to shortCacheTTL (30s), creating a privilege-revocation bypass window that did not exist when Check always queried the DB. HOW: Revalidate revocations before trusting cached allow, or shorten/invalidate permCache on permission changes.

WHAT: List serves whatever scopeMap is in permCache without the per-item DB fallback that Check has. WHY: Newly granted dashboards/folders stay invisible (and revoked ones stay listed) until permCache TTL expires, regressing List from always-fresh getIdentityPermissions to stale reads and contradicting the PR goal. HOW: Apply the same miss/outdated fallback for List or bypass permCache for List.

WHAT: Check short-circuits to deny on permDenialCache hit without requerying permissions. WHY: A denial cached at line 154 is never cleared when permissions are later granted, so a newly granted resource is still denied until shortCacheTTL expiry, reintroducing the staleness the cached-perms fallback was meant to fix. HOW: Invalidate/delete the denial key when fresh permissions grant the resource, or do not short-circuit and always attempt the cached-perms then DB fallback.

WHAT: Every denied Check inserts a distinct denial entry keyed by (namespace,user,action,name,parent) via userPermDenialCacheKey. WHY: Name/parent are request-controlled with unbounded cardinality, so enumerating random resources fills the shared cache with single-use denial keys until expiry, growing memory and evicting useful entries. HOW: Bound denial-cache cardinality (e.g. only cache denies for known resources, limit size, or use a negative cache with coarse keys).

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.
Claims permissionCacheUsage counts a cache hit that did not grant access as a cache miss.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: immediateDelete path POSTs cancel to SendGrid then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: Leaves an orphan scheduled=true row after workflow/step delete and reschedule callers (workflows.tsx:214,521 handleNewBooking.ts:968) so DB claims scheduled while SendGrid is cancelled. HOW: Delete the prisma row after successful cancel when immediateDelete is true.

issues.descricao: The booking-page reschedule path cancels email reminders with immediateDelete=true, which leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB, while the dashboard reschedule path marks it cancelled for cleanup, so the two flows are inconsistent.
Claims the code comment overstates the cancel window because the query lacks a lower bound on scheduledDate.
Claims the cron's cancel loop uses an undefined `client` variable, causing a ReferenceError.
Claims the unscheduled-reminders query re-schedules reminders marked cancelled because it lacks a cancelled filter.
Claims a hard-coded "Verification code" placeholder bypasses i18n.
Claims a hard-coded "Verify" button label bypasses i18n.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid send but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, leaving orphaned scheduled rows inconsistent with the non-immediate path.
Claims reminders from disabled event types are still sent and can be re-scheduled because they are only marked cancelled.
Notes the isSenderIdNeeded branch removal without reporting a problem.
The new cancelled column is nullable without a default, so existing WorkflowReminder rows get null instead of false.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row, and the callers no longer delete it, so reminder rows are left orphaned in the database.
The reschedule path cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately (immediateDelete=true) instead of flagging them cancelled for the cron, which supposedly accumulates cancelled batches.
When an email reminder is cancelled immediately on reschedule, its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so stale scheduled reminder rows are left in the database.
Claims the cron's cancelled-reminders query can pick rows with a null referenceId and send batch_id:null to SendGrid, aborting cancellation of the remaining reminders.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Errors-dataset queries are enabled for upsampling but upsampled_count is only registered on DiscoverDatasetConfig. WHY: Errors-dataset timeseries/top-events calls will resolve an unknown function and fail or fall back incorrectly when allowlisted. HOW: Register upsampled_count for the errors dataset config too, or gate errors dataset off until supported.

issues.descricao: The test factory helper uses a truthiness check on client_sample_rate, so a rate of 0.0 is not copied to sample_rate (claimed to silently drop a legitimate value).
Claims cache keys for upsampling eligibility are built with Python's hash() and cannot be invalidated across workers; no such cache exists.
Claims changing the topEvents validation message breaks consumers asserting the old 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' text; none exist.
Comment reports no problem.
Comment reports no problem.
Comment reports no problem.
Comment reports no problem.
Claims the factory writes sample_rate while upsampled_count reads sample_weight, so the upsampled count would be 1 instead of 10.
upsampled_count is registered only in DiscoverDatasetConfig, so if the errors dataset resolves functions through another config, the upsampled_count() query fails as an unknown function.
Inline test comments say each bucket has 1 event while the assertions expect count == 10, contradicting the upsampled value.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: _get_partition_lock creates per-partition locks via unsynchronized get+setdefault on partition_locks dict. WHY: concurrent add_offset (submit thread) and complete_offset/get_committable (worker/commit threads) for a new Partition can create two different Lock objects and mutate all_offsets/outstanding dict structure without protection, breaking the claimed thread-safety and risking lost updates or RuntimeError during list(all_offsets.keys()). HOW: guard lock creation/all_offsets structure mutation with a global lock.

issues.descricao: Claims queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() are unavailable on Python < 3.13, so workers never exit on shutdown.
Claims Python's randomized str hash makes group-to-queue assignment differ across processes, breaking per-subscription ordering and letting two processes handle the same subscription concurrently.
Claims FixedQueuePool.submit leaks an outstanding offset when put() raises after add_offset, permanently blocking commits for the partition.
Claims get_stats/wait_until_empty report empty while items are still in flight because qsize drops when a worker takes an item.
Claims metrics.incr receives len(committable) as the instance argument instead of the amount, so the commit count is always 1.
The offsets_committed metric is incremented by the number of partitions being committed rather than the number of offsets, so its name misdescribes the value.
Claims factory shutdown leaves SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads running and committing after shutdown.
Claims the committable-offset loop iterates the whole numeric span max_offset - start, burning CPU on large offset gaps every commit cycle.
_get_partition_lock reads and writes partition_locks without a global lock, claimed to let two threads create different locks for one partition and break offset tracking.
States review of queue_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.
States review of result_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Topic#unsubscribe_url returns a relative path interpolated into email markdown via user_notifications.rb unsubscribe_url. WHY: Email clients cannot resolve a relative href so the per-topic unsubscribe link in notification emails is broken.

WHAT: Shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but other senders using add_unsubscribe_link do not supply it. WHY: Raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or renders a broken link for every other email type that uses the unsubscribe footer.

WHAT: New topicUnsubscribe route at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe collides with existing topic.fromParamsNear /:nearPost route which matches any string including 'unsubscribe'. WHY: Navigation to the unsubscribe URL can resolve to the topic post-stream route with nearPost='unsubscribe' instead of the unsubscribe template, loading the wrong page and feeding a non-numeric nearPost into closestPostForPostNumber/refresh logic. HOW: Define the unsubscribe route before the topic resource, constrain :nearPost to numeric/last, or use a distinct path that cannot match :nearPost.

issues.descricao: Claims other mailers using add_unsubscribe_link do not pass unsubscribe_url, so rendering unsubscribe_link raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument.
Claims the unsubscribe page renders the topic title unescaped through triple braces, allowing HTML injection.
Claims the per-topic unsubscribe URL in emails is relative and cannot be resolved by email clients.
Claims the topicUnsubscribe route cannot find its template because the template lives at topic/unsubscribe.hbs.
The per-topic unsubscribe link in notification emails is built from a relative topic URL, so it has no scheme or host and cannot be opened from mail clients.
The unsubscribe_link string now requires unsubscribe_url, so any MessageBuilder caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without it would raise a missing-interpolation error.
Claims unsubscribe serializes the stale notification level because TopicView memoized topic_user before the update.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: New getCredentials() dereferences myUser without a null check (myUser.recoveryCodes). WHY: Throws NPE for unknown/removed users during federated credential lookup, crashing authentication where sibling methods (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) explicitly null-guard. HOW: Return Stream.empty() when getMyUser(user) is null before touching fields.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.
Claims recovery code verification compares hashes with String.equals, enabling timing attacks.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Direct val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError when the field is absent. WHY: One old/malformed SpanEvent crashes the whole process_batch batch instead of skipping/defaulting. HOW: Use val.get("end_timestamp_precise") with a fallback (e.g., now/timestamp) or validate and drop the span.

issues.descricao: Claims the redirect-resolution limit was silently cut from 10000 to 1000, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined, and the comment still mentions 10k.
Claims a non-root span whose key equals the resolved set key unions the key with itself and then unlinks it, deleting the buffered segment.
Claims a span message missing end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and aborts the whole batch.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch passes cursor.offset directly into queryset slicing when advanced features are enabled.
Claims BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset to an unclamped offset for previous-page cursors, allowing negative slicing.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies floor/ceil to a datetime key, raising TypeError.
Claims accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when organization_context is None.
process_batch indexes end_timestamp_precise directly, so a span without the field raises KeyError and fails the whole consumer batch.
Claims span_count counts pre-existing spans in set_key, so zpopmin evicts far more than the overflow above 1000 and discards valid spans.
SDK-supplied end_timestamp_precise is used as the ZSET eviction score, so an attacker sending far-future timestamps could keep their spans and force eviction of legitimate ones.
Each span insert runs up to two ZUNIONSTORE copies of the segment set plus ZCARD/ZPOPMIN, making segment building O(N^2) on the ingest hot path.
Claims end_timestamp_precise is not validated as finite before being used as a ZADD score.
Claims test_backpressure uses identical end_timestamp_precise values and so cannot catch timestamp-ordering or eviction regressions.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Same-domain website_name is built as website_host + URI(website).path, dropping query string, fragment, and port (and not normalizing case). WHY: A same-domain URL like http://example.com/user?tab=about#bio displays as example.com/user, losing the distinguishing path and showing wrong/truncated output contrary to complete-path intent.

issues.descricao: The www.example.com vs forum.example.com branch of website_name is not tested.
The scheme-less website case (nil host) of website_name is not tested.
Claims the suffix check `"." << website_host` mutates website_host by prepending a dot, so unrelated domains are displayed as ".example.com" and the new unrelated-domain spec fails.
website_name parses the website with URI and returns nil when there is no scheme, so a website like example.com/user disappears from the profile.
The same-domain website label concatenates only host and path, dropping the query string and fragment so the label differs from the link.
Claims website_name silently swallows URI parse errors without logging.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: New getForLogin cache has no invalidation on removeAll() (which only invalidates the count key). WHY: After removeAll the cached IdentityProviderListQuery per FetchMode still returns the old internalIds, serving deleted brokers as login options until natural eviction. HOW: Call registerIDPLoginInvalidation-equivalent (invalidate all FetchMode login keys) in removeAll().

WHAT: New getLoginPredicate() clause dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without null-guarding getConfig(). WHY: A programmatically built IdentityProviderModel with null config (or null config map from storage) throws NPE in every getForLogin/invalidation path that evaluates the predicate, breaking login rendering. HOW: Null-guard the config map before get(), e.g. idp.getConfig() != null && Boolean.parseBoolean(...).

WHAT: Cache miss for a new organizationId calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), evicting all already-cached org searches for that FetchMode cluster-wide. WHY: Each distinct org login view invalidates and rewrites the shared per-mode entry, causing cache thrashing and redundant idpDelegate.getForLogin DB loads that grow with organization count. HOW: Merge the new searchKey without a full invalidate (revisioned put), mirroring append-only semantics.

WHAT: The new getForLogin cache (key realmId+.idp.login.+mode, per-org searchKeys) is never invalidated when an IDP is linked/unlinked to an organization via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider. WHY: Those methods (InfinispanOrganizationProvider:250-270) only register organization invalidation, so cached REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL ID sets stay stale — a newly linked IDP still appears in REALM_ONLY and is missing from ORG_ONLY (and vice-versa on unlink), showing wrong login brokers. HOW: Invalidate all FetchMode login keys for the realm when organization-IDP membership changes (or hook registerIDPLoginInvalidation into the organization provider path).

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.
Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.
Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.
Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.
Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.
Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.
Claims org-specific ALL/ORG_ONLY login queries include non-public org IDPs, so the BROKER_PUBLIC gate misses invalidations; the query always requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true.

getForLogin caches all organizations under one realm/mode entry, so each new organizationId invalidates and rebuilds that entry with every previously cached search merged in, instead of caching per organization.

Disabling an organization does not invalidate the cached login IDP lists in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin, so callers that do not re-check isEnabled could get IDPs of a disabled organization.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: resourceStore.findByName passes server.getId() as ownerId instead of server.getClientId(). WHY: Resources are created with owner resourceServer.getClientId() (AdminPermissionsSchema:104) and the default finder uses getClientId(), so the 3-arg lookup never matches and per-client permissions are never found, forcing incorrect fallback to all-clients. HOW: Pass server.getClientId() or use the 2-arg findByName overload like UserPermissionsV2 does.

WHAT: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled on ClientRemovedEvent. WHY: Deleting any client when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 routes management() to MgmtPermissionsV2 will throw from the event listener and fail client removal. HOW: Guard the listener for V2 or make V2 setPermissionsEnabled a no-op.

WHAT: hasPermission accepts any returned Permission scope without checking permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()). WHY: UserPermissionsV2 filters by resourceId, but this code grants if any evaluated permission contains the scope, so a grant attached to a different resource evaluated together (typed/all-clients resource via DefaultPolicyEvaluator) can authorize the wrong client — authorization bypass. HOW: Filter by resource id like UserPermissionsV2 does, while still allowing the type-resource grant when intended.

WHAT: getClientsWithPermission calls evaluatePermission once per client resource inside findByType iteration. WHY: Client listing/filtering therefore costs O(N) full policy evaluations where N is the number of client resources in the realm, a material slowdown on large realms. HOW: Batch evaluation or query policies/scopes without per-resource full evaluation if possible.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.
Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.
Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.
ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation for every client resource of type Clients, so listing clients costs one evaluation per client resource.

On ClientRemovedEvent the AdminPermissions listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 when V1 and V2 are both enabled, so client deletion fails.
Claims that with both fine-grained authz V1 and V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws, so client deletion fails.
Claims the test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so addComposites may succeed because of CONFIGURE and the test would pass even if canMapCompositeRoles were broken.
Claims that under FGAP V2 the client management-permissions GET/PUT endpoints call the throwing ClientPermissionsV2 overrides and return 500.

ClientPermissionsV2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles check only fine-grained permissions and not the manage-clients role, claimed to deny role mapping to realm admins unlike V1.
Claims the canView(ClientModel) Javadoc is misleading because V2 never evaluates the per-client VIEW_SCOPE permission.
Claims the tests index getDefaultClientScopes() without size checks and could throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: handleAdd validates raw multiEmailValue including empty placeholder rows (initialized as [""] and appended by Add-another). WHY: any untouched empty row fails the z.string().email() check, so adding multiple guests with a blank row rejects otherwise-valid emails. HOW: filter out empty/whitespace entries before safeParse and mutate, e.g. const emails = multiEmailValue.filter((e) => e.trim() !== "").

issues.descricao: Claims newGuests.includes(attendee.email) misroutes newly added guests whose casing differs from the stored value, but new attendees are stored with exactly the submitted string.
Suggests starting with [] instead of [""] because the empty string may cause validation issues; the empty initial field is intentional and validated.
sendAddGuestsEmails never notifies the newly added guests because the formatted event does not contain them, so the newGuests branch is unreachable.
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail reads calEvent.attendees[0].name without a guard and throws when the attendee list is empty.
The AddGuests dialog error toast shows the raw server error message and code, which could display internal backend details such as Prisma errors to the user.
Swallowing email-sending errors returns success even if notification emails fail; the failure should be surfaced to the UI.
Claims the organizer add-guests email subject uses attendees[0].name, which becomes empty because newly added guests are stored with an empty name.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: santizeAnchors only iterates anchors found in the translation and never checks for English anchors missing from it, and continues iterating a stale matcher after mutating value via replaceFirst. WHY: A translation that drops an opening or closing <a> tag passes silently (returned value has anchors stripped, later HTML check sees no tags), breaking links without a verifier error and mis-attributing subsequent matches.

issues.descricao: Claims santizeAnchors consumes English matcher groups without validation, so a translation with more anchor tags than the English text gets incorrect results.
Notes that normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged.
Claims the English-file path rewrite is fragile and that a messages file without an English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException.
Notes no test covers allowed tags under POLICY_SOME_HTML, so emptying the allow-list would not fail the suite.
VerifyMessageProperties loads message bundles with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), claimed to decode as ISO-8859-1 and produce mojibake and spurious Illegal HTML failures for non-English files.
The message verifier compares English files against themselves, so any anchor tag in an English source, including an unsafe href, is stripped before the HTML sanitizer check and never reported.
Error messages in the verifier include absolute file paths; the comment states no data-exposure defect was found.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: updateDevice restricts the UPDATE with WHERE updated_at BETWEEN [now-30d, now+1m], so an existing device whose row went stale (>30d) matches 0 rows and is misreported as ErrDeviceLimitReached. WHY: A known device cannot re-register once expired when the table is at limit, diverging from the upsert path used when under limit. HOW: Match only on device_id for existing devices (update regardless of updated_at age), and return limit-reached only when the device_id truly does not exist.

WHAT: ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a deviceLimit int64 parameter but pkg/server/wire.go:374 still registers it as a wire provider with no int64 binding. WHY: Wire cannot inject a primitive int64, so generation/build breaks or creates a duplicate store with an unresolved limit; the service now builds the store manually in impl.go:43 making the wire provider stale. HOW: Remove anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore (and its AnonStore binding if unused) from the wire set or provide a named int64/cfg-derived constructor.

WHAT: anonymousDeviceLimit is declared as `= undefined` with no type annotation while GrafanaConfig requires `number | undefined`. WHY: The property infers type `undefined` only (cf. loginError which annotates `string | undefined`), so assigning the numeric backend value fails type-checking/leaves the frontend limit unusable. HOW: Declare `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.
Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.
Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.
Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit parameter but is still registered as a wire provider in pkg/server/wire.go, which has no provider for int64, so wire generation or compilation fails.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit but is still registered as a Wire provider (with an AnonStore bind) in pkg/server/wire.go; Wire cannot supply an int64, so DI generation and the server build fail.
Claims updateDevice's RowsAffected()==0 check wrongly denies already-registered devices on MySQL because MySQL reports changed rather than matched rows.
CreateOrUpdateDevice runs a full COUNT over the 30-day anon_device table on every anonymous request when a device limit is set.
The 'device limit reached' error string is hard-coded English and bypasses i18n.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Create passes the original input obj to Legacy.Create instead of the storage-returned created object while sharing the same mutable pointer across a goroutine. WHY: Storage-assigned defaults/resourceVersion are lost in legacy and concurrent mutation/access is a data race. HOW: Pass created (or a deep copy of it) to the legacy goroutine.

WHAT: Create/Get/List/Delete/Update dereference options.Kind (and List/DeleteCollection deref listOptions) without nil check. WHY: A nil options call that previously succeeded now panics with nil dereference. HOW: Guard nil options/listOptions before WithValues or default the kind label.

issues.descricao: Claims the Equal/NotEqual assertions in the Mode 3 tests can never fail, though the Equal assertion does fail if Delete stops returning the storage result.
Claims the legacy-create goroutine races with the caller on a shared obj that can alias the returned object.
Empty comment.
Every mode-3 write spawns an unbounded goroutine for the legacy store, risking goroutine and memory growth under load.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: attacker-controlled request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted JS string. WHY: a Referer containing ' or </script> breaks out and executes as reflected XSS in the Discourse origin inside the framed page. HOW: encode with escape_javascript/to_json and use only the origin.

WHAT: parent.postMessage uses full request.referer as targetOrigin instead of the origin. WHY: targetOrigin must be scheme://host[:port] or *, so a full URL with path never matches and resize messages are silently dropped. HOW: pass request.protocol+host / origin only.

WHAT: code dereferences document.getElementById('discourse-comments') without a null check before appendChild. WHY: pages missing that container throw and abort the embed script. HOW: return early if comments is null.

WHAT: poll_feed loops over all rss.items with a DB lookup plus PostCreator/PostRevisor transaction per item and no limit. WHY: a large feed retriggered hourly (and synchronously from TopicRetriever) causes unbounded hourly write/query blowup and job timeouts. HOW: limit items, order newest-first with early break on unchanged sha.

WHAT: spec expects EmbedController#best to call TopicRetriever.new/retrieve directly while the controller enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic). WHY: the mock expectation is never satisfied so the newly added test fails and does not cover the actual async path. HOW: expect Jobs.enqueue with embed_url instead of TopicRetriever.new.

issues.descricao: Claims embed.js throws a TypeError when the page lacks the #discourse-comments element because comments.appendChild is called on null.
Claims the embed controller spec fails because EmbedController#best only enqueues a Sidekiq job and never constructs TopicRetriever during the request.
The hourly PollFeed job always fetches and processes the full feed without a conditional GET; the feed_key helper meant for that is defined but never used.
States that the link fallback in PollFeed is correct; no problem is reported.
States the raw_html cook_method comparison in Post#cook is safe; no problem is reported.
States the cook_method assignment in PostCreator is correct; no problem is reported.
States the `if topic_id` check in EmbedController is safe; no problem is reported.
Describes the host checks in ensure_embeddable without reporting a problem.
States content_sha1 and absolutize_urls in TopicEmbed are correct; no problem is reported.
States the TopicRetriever throttle uses setnx and an explicit no_throttle check; no problem is reported.
Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.
Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.
Claims postMessage drops the resize message because targetOrigin is the full referer URL rather than just the origin, breaking iframe auto-resize.
Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.
Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.
`<%- end if %>` in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby, so the template raises a SyntaxError and the embed page fails to render.
Claims `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling if modifier that makes the logo output the condition, so the logo renders before the header button.
Claims the embed best action builds the view for current_user and then marks it publicly cacheable, so a staff member's view could be served to anonymous visitors.
fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence check, raising NoMethodError when the setting is blank.
poll_feed opens the feed URL without a timeout and imports every item without a cap, so a slow or huge feed can tie up a worker.
The TopicRetriever specs mock perform_retrieve, so a bug in invalid_host? would not make them fail.
The EmbedController success tests only assert that mocks are called and would pass even if the controller logic were removed.
poll_feed has no test of feed parsing or TopicEmbed.import; the specs only check the execute guards.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Base `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound` adds `assignment_source` kwarg but the `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` override accepts no **kwargs and no status-path caller was updated to thread it. WHY: Calling the override via the new base contract with assignment_source raises TypeError, and status sync cycles remain unfiltered because the param is always None.

issues.descricao: Claims to_dict() returns a raw datetime for queued that fails JSON serialization when passed as Celery task kwargs.
The assignment_source parameter was added to the abstract sync_status_outbound instead of sync_assignee_outbound, which is the method that actually receives it.
Claims concrete integrations overriding should_sync(self, attribute) will raise TypeError at the new two-argument call in sync_assignee_outbound.
Claims a malformed assignment_source_dict makes from_dict return None, so should_sync fails open and re-enables the sync cycle.
test_to_dict asserts queued is not None, which is always true because queued has a default, so the assertion verifies nothing.
Claims passing AssignmentSource.to_dict() with a raw datetime to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async fails Sentry's bad-pickle check in tests and would break under a JSON serializer.

sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that is never threaded through the status task or checked in should_sync, so status sync gets no cycle prevention despite the signature suggesting it.
The base sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter but ExampleIntegration's override takes no **kwargs, so callers passing assignment_source would raise TypeError.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: API URL download cap changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to hardcoded `10.megabytes`. WHY: Lets a remote URL force the server (SSRF-adjacent sink `FileHelper.download`) to fetch/store up to 10MB even when admin capped images much lower, bypassing admin limit and amplifying bandwidth/disk exhaustion via API uploads. HOW: Restore `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap (or max(configured, downsizable ceiling)) for the download.

issues.descricao: Claims the API URL download limit changed from max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10 MB, amplifying SSRF bandwidth.
Downsizing uses the same path as input and output for ImageMagick convert, which can corrupt or truncate the upload.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host]/[:category_id] with no require/presence check. WHY: missing or malformed embeddable_host param raises NoMethodError on nil instead of 400/validation error. HOW: use params.require(:embeddable_host) with permitted keys and handle missing values.

WHAT: expandable_first_post? dropped the embeddable-hosts-present check and now only checks embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?. WHY: returns true for truncated embeds even when the embeddable_hosts table is empty, re-enabling expansion with no allowed hosts (old spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes vacuously). HOW: also require EmbeddableHost.exists? (or equivalent).

WHAT: eh = record_for_host(url) can be nil/false (host deleted or normalization mismatch) and category: eh.try(:category_id) then passes nil, unlike the controller fallback to uncategorized_category_id. WHY: PostCreator receives nil category for an embed that passed earlier checks, creating miscategorized or failed topics. HOW: fall back to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id when eh/category is blank.

WHAT: plural branch calls obj[k].map(...) assuming *_ids is always an array. WHY: a null/undefined/singleton ids payload throws TypeError and breaks hydration for that record. HOW: guard Array.isArray(obj[k]) before mapping, defaulting to [].

issues.descricao: Claims expandable_first_post? lost its 'embeddable hosts configured' guard and now expands first posts when no EmbeddableHost exists.
Claims the plural *_ids hydration branch crashes on non-array values and keeps undefined entries for missing ids.
Claims Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing, so the client's saveChanges appears to succeed without saving.
Claims EmbeddingSerializer emits only embeddable_host_ids without sideloading the host records, so the admin host table renders empty.

_hydrateEmbedded now treats every `_ids` key as an embedded collection: it calls `.map` without a null/array check (TypeError on null) and always deletes the original key, replacing real id arrays with undefined lookups when the root has no matching collection.
RestAdapter.basePath replaces only the first underscore of the model type, so an admin model type with several underscores would not match ADMIN_MODELS and would use the wrong base path.
EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false on bad input and TopicEmbed.import calls eh.try(:category_id), which is claimed to raise on FalseClass and crash the import for malformed URLs.
Embed host checks now issue a database query via EmbeddableHost.record_for_host on every embed request instead of the previous in-memory site-setting check.
TopicEmbed.import passes a nil category when no embeddable host matches the URL, dropping the old embed_category default.
save_host replaces category_id 0 with the uncategorized category because it uses blank? instead of nil?.
The host input placeholder 'example.com' is hard-coded instead of using I18n.
The EmbeddableHostsController spec only checks inheritance and does not exercise create, update or destroy.
The EmbeddingController spec only checks inheritance and does not exercise show or update.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym without nil guard, crashing when default_locale is nil/unloaded. WHY: The PR description itself states default_locale is not guaranteed loaded at boot, so the first fallback resolution raises NoMethodError on nil instead of falling back to :en. HOW: Use SiteSetting.default_locale.try(:to_sym) / safe navigation so compact can drop nil.

WHAT: New I18n.ensure_loaded! forwards attacker-influenced locale (User#effective_locale -> self.locale, unchecked) into load_locale which builds Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$") without escaping. WHY: A locale containing regex metacharacters (e.g. ".*") changes which load_path entries match and get loaded, enabling load amplification / ReDoS via crafted profile locale. HOW: Escape with Regexp.escape(locale.to_s) and validate locale against LocaleSiteSetting.supported_locales before loading.

WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] performs a SiteSetting.default_locale lookup on every fallback resolution. WHY: With fallbacks enabled the backend consults fallbacks[locale] per translate/miss, turning hundreds of per-request translates into hundreds of settings lookups and slowing the hot translation path. HOW: Memoize/cache default_locale per request or compute fallback chain once per locale change instead of per key.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.
Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.
Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.
Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.
Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
I18n.ensure_loaded! reads and initializes @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, racing with reload!/load_locale under concurrent requests.
Claims set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (application_controller.rb:159) raises NoMethodError on every request if I18n.fallbacks is not the custom FallbackLocaleList.
FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves it empty, so iterating I18n.fallbacks returns nothing.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: reader thread tight-loops groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) with no sleep/backoff while deletes run. WHY: each iteration requests unbounded full top-level group list, hammering server/DB in a hot spin and slowing the suite. HOW: page with a bounded maxResults and add a small sleep/yield or iteration cap.

issues.descricao: GroupAdapter's NPE guard is applied only to getSubGroupsCount; the getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference modelSupplier.get(), which is null when the group is deleted concurrently.
The concurrency test's reader thread busy-loops full group listings with maxResults=Integer.MAX_VALUE and no throttle, claimed to overload the server and destabilise the suite.
The reader thread catches only Exception, so Errors thrown during concurrent reads are swallowed and the test passes anyway.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Booking create persists only evt.destinationCalendar[0].id while creation fans out to all evt.destinationCalendar entries. WHY: Reschedule/cancel/reject reload booking.destinationCalendar (single FK) so events created on co-hosts' calendars are never updated/deleted, leaving orphan calendar events and inconsistent state. HOW: Persist all destinations (e.g. join table or store each createdEvent externalId/credentialId reference) instead of connecting only the first entry.

issues.descricao: Claims GoogleCalendarService.createEvent/updateEvent dereference an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
destinationCalendar is defaulted to null in some producers and to an empty array in others.
loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic-user bookings, so code reading user.organization gets undefined.

Claims that for references without a credentialId, looping over every calendar reference and deleting each against all user calendar credentials produces duplicate or wrong-target delete calls and errors.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: add_members splits usernames on comma without stripping whitespace, so 'user1, user2' looks up ' user2' via User.find_by_username and silently skips it. WHY: user-selector input joins with commas/spaces so the second and later usernames fail to be added with no error. HOW: strip each token (username.strip or username.strip!) before lookup and skip blanks.

WHAT: add_members/remove_member read params.require(:group_id) but the routes define member routes (/admin/groups/:id/members) so the id arrives as params[:id], not params[:group_id]. WHY: Real requests from group.js (`/admin/groups/:id/members.json`) raise ActionController::ParameterMissing and member add/remove is broken; specs pass only because they inject group_id directly bypassing routing. HOW: Read the id the route provides (e.g. Group.find(params[:id] || params[:group_id])) or declare the routes as collection/with explicit :group_id segment.

issues.descricao: Claims the now-unawaited findMembers() call creates a race where the controller has no member data available when it needs it.
Claims the public group members template iterates a bare members property that resolves to undefined because the controller's model is now the Group object.
Claims add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] while the route supplies the group id as params[:id], so the actions always fail with ParameterMissing.
Claims add_members does not strip whitespace around comma-separated usernames, so entries like 'alice, bob' silently fail to add members.
Claims the public members endpoint accepts an unbounded or negative limit/offset, letting a caller force loading and serializing the whole membership of a large group.
params[:alias_level].present? is false for 0, so choosing the 'nobody' alias level is ignored.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on a throwaway LoginFormsProvider from context.form() that is never rendered. WHY: context.form() creates a new provider per call (AuthenticationProcessor.java:589-612), and both callers render with a different instance — WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse uses at least 3 distinct context.form() calls (setError, setup, fillContextForm, errorChallenge) and badPasswordHandler renders via challenge() with a fresh instance — so after a passkey/password error during re-auth the flags are lost, falling back to editable-username regular login. HOW: Set the attributes on the same provider instance used to render (e.g., return/pass the form or set them after fillContextForm inside the rendering path).

issues.descricao: Claims PasswordForm.authenticate can fill passkey context data for a null user because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled returns true when no user is set, producing an inconsistent password page.
Claims configuredFor marks PasswordForm as configured for passkey-only users, so they land on a password form they cannot satisfy.
Claims action() processes a passkey assertion for a different userHandle during re-authentication, letting another user's passkey satisfy re-auth of the fixed user.
Claims the password page leaks the typed user's passkey credential IDs to an unauthenticated visitor, disclosing whether the account has passkeys.
Claims a Kotlin state manager should use ViewModel + StateFlow for UI state.
Claims UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the required UserModel argument.
Claims isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, so the initial login page no longer sets up conditional passkey UI for ID-less login.
Reports that widening USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH and the reauth form helper expose no sensitive data.
Reports that setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only toggles UI flags and leaks nothing.
Reports that the passkey conditional-UI data is non-secret; no exposure.
Reports that the added error-path calls leak no credential information.
Reports that emitting WebAuthn credential IDs in passkeys.ftl is not sensitive.
Reports that the auth note writer and reader use the same key; refactor is behaviour-preserving.
Reports that the helper reads the same auth note key.
Reports that the constant's value is unchanged by the visibility change.
Reports that isConditionalPasskeysEnabled is reused consistently.
Reports no issue at UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate.
Reports no issue at UsernamePasswordForm.challenge.
Reports no issue at PasswordForm.authenticate.
Reports no issue at PasswordForm.configuredFor.
Reports no unreachable branch in action().
Reports no NPE in PasswordForm.authenticate because the helper checks webauthnAuth != null.
Reports no computed-then-ignored values.
States the authn_use_chk field name could not be checked against the JavaScript; no problem asserted.

The password page now renders an identified user's passkey credential IDs as hidden inputs in the username-first flow before authentication, disclosing credential metadata to anyone who knows a username.

After a username-only step, PasswordForm fills WebAuthn context for the user and passkeys.ftl renders their credential IDs as hidden inputs, letting an unauthenticated visitor learn whether an account has a passkey and its credential IDs.
No test exercises a passkey failure during re-authentication, so the new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator is never covered.

setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError sets attributes on a fresh context.form() instance that is claimed to be discarded, so the re-authentication error page loses the hidden-username state.
Claims the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH comment is stale because the flag no longer governs user clearing.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Context caches grantType at construction from formParams but setFormParams() replaces formParams without refreshing the cached grantType. WHY: Any caller mutating form params leaves getGrantType() stale, so OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse stores the wrong Constants.GRANT_TYPE and the token-id prefix encodes the wrong grant. HOW: Update grantType inside setFormParams (or compute getGrantType() lazily from current formParams).

WHAT: initToken unconditionally dereferences session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for unknown grantType. WHY: Token issuance that previously always succeeded with a UUID now fails with NPE (provider missing) or 500 (unregistered/custom grant string from formParams) for flows that never set a mapped GRANT_TYPE. HOW: Fall back to KeycloakModelUtils.generateId() when encoder is null or shortcut is unknown.

issues.descricao: Claims setFormParams replaces form params without refreshing the cached grantType, leaving getGrantType() stale.
getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation, breaking existing custom grant type factories when the encoder factory calls it.
Token context encoding calls getShouldUseLightweightToken on every token creation, which dereferences the session context client and would NPE where no client is set.
initToken always encodes the token id and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for a grant type without a registered shortcut, so custom or unmapped grants would fail token issuance with a 500.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Pause/Delete/Duplicate/Silence/Export permissions are OR-combined between ruler abilities and new grafana prom abilities, while provisioned detection for prom path depends on optional promRule.provenance. WHY: If prom DTO omits provenance, isProvisionedPromRule is false so the grafana side reports editable/removable and the OR grants Edit/Delete/Pause on provisioned immutable rules that the ruler path would deny. HOW: Require both sides to agree on immutability or fall back to denied when provenance is unknown.

WHAT: Loader now renders only promResponse groups and dropped the ruler query plus matchRules Creating/Deleting branches. WHY: Ruler-only (newly creating) rules disappear from the list and prom-only (deleting) rules now render as normal editable rules with Edit/More instead of Deleting placeholders. HOW: Restore ruler fetch with matchRules or explicitly handle creating/deleting states from prom-only data.

issues.descricao: Claims provisioned status now comes from promRule.provenance, which the Prometheus response might omit, making provisioned rules editable.
Claims the promRule prop typed as Rule makes the Grafana prom-rule type guard return false for the GrafanaPromRuleDTO passed by GrafanaRuleListItem.
The menu test asserts exactly 4 menu items although the menuItems map also includes delete, so the count or comment may not match the real menu.
GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only Prometheus rules and drops the ruler matching, so rules being created disappear and rules being deleted show as normal rows with full actions.
The optional chain stops at .rules, so an empty groups array is claimed to call undefined.map() and throw.
The comment says location is redundant, but showLocation={false} is claimed not to be passed, so grouped rules would show the location.
Using promRule.uid as React key could clash if uids are not unique within a group.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: JSON.parse(req.query.state) throws on attacker-controlled malformed state with no try/catch. WHY: Any crafted /api/integrations/*/callback?state=not-json crashes the handler with 500 instead of 400. HOW: Wrap in try/catch and return undefined or throw HttpError 400.

WHAT: Team credential creation only checks accepted membership, not admin role, while non-team path enforces throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam. WHY: Any accepted team member can mint team-level OAuth credentials by crafting state.teamId, escalating to team-wide integration access. HOW: Require admin/owner check for teamId path too.

WHAT: Decrypted keys are JSON.parse'd with no schema validation and written directly to credential.key for arbitrary userId/appSlug. WHY: Holder of the shared webhook secret (or leaked secret) can inject malformed credential JSON that later crashes schema parses or hijacks integrations for any user. HOW: Validate keys against per-app credential schema before create/update and reject on mismatch.

WHAT: Sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortSignal, no error handling, and runs in the hot token-refresh path for every calendar/video call. WHY: A slow or down sync endpoint blocks availability/booking flows until default fetch timeout, causing material latency blowup per request. HOW: Add AbortSignal.timeout and fall back to refreshFunction on failure.

issues.descricao: Claims the JSDoc describes appData.type as 'the app slug', copied from appData.appId.
Claims the team-credential branch only checks accepted membership instead of admin rights, letting non-admin members create team credentials.
Claims malformed OAuth state makes JSON.parse throw and crash OAuth callbacks with a 500.
Claims the Office365 video adapter passes the wrong app slug 'msteams' to refreshOAuthTokens.
createOAuthAppCredential only verifies team membership, not admin access, before creating a team credential, so any team member can install OAuth apps for the team via a crafted state.
The app-credential webhook decrypts keys with CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY falling back to an empty string when the env var is unset, instead of failing fast.
The app-credential webhook is claimed to accept GET, so a loggable, prefetchable, CSRF-able request carrying the shared secret could overwrite any user's stored OAuth keys.
The app-credential webhook authenticates only by a static shared-secret header, so whoever holds the secret can overwrite any user's app credentials without per-user auth, HMAC or replay protection.
The .env.example tells users to generate CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which is claimed to give only 24 bytes instead of the 32 required by AES256.
The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout, so a hanging endpoint could block calendar/video requests.
The truthy userId check treats user id 0 as absent and skips the credential sync endpoint.
Claims decrypted credential keys are stored without validation against the app's credential schema, allowing credential poisoning if the webhook secret is compromised.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: order() passes $val unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, which are 1-indexed while order is 0-indexed. WHY: @include order(2)/order(3) in topic.scss/header.scss render one position off on legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box browsers, misordering header panel vs extra-info. HOW: add 1 for the old box model, e.g. -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
Making .small-action a flex container is claimed to make the floated buttons ignore float:right, because they would be flex items, so they collapse next to the description.
Claims that removing the 5px bullet margin in .extra-info-wrapper misaligns category bullets because the wrapper's parent is still float-based and order() has no effect.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware reuses a single shared *MetricsMiddleware and mutates imw.next on every CreateClientMiddleware call. WHY: Decorator.clientFromMiddlewares rebuilds the chain per request, so concurrent requests concurrently write/read imw.next causing a data race and potentially routing through another request's downstream chain. HOW: Allocate a new MetricsMiddleware per call (copy pluginMetrics/registry, set next) like ContextualLoggerMiddleware/LoggerMiddleware do.

WHAT: logRequest dropped explicit pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname/traceID fields and now relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). WHY: Those fields only appear if upstream NewContextualLoggerMiddleware ran and global contextual/trace providers are registered, so standalone use or reordering of LoggerMiddleware silently loses plugin/request identity in logs. HOW: Keep explicit fields or document/enforce the ordering dependency.

issues.descricao: Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests because it reads req.PluginContext without a nil guard.
Claims the refactor dropped traceID from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines.
Claims the metrics middleware factory mutates a shared instance's next field, causing a data race between chains.
Claims the request-size histogram's HELP text says 'returned' though it measures request sizes.
Claims the test never asserts that request size is not instrumented for CheckHealth/CollectMetrics.
Claims checkHistogram carries foundLabels across metrics and returns errors prematurely.
Claims millisecond durations are truncated by integer division before conversion to float.
Claims the request-size test cases use empty payloads and would not detect a broken size calculation.
Claims the duration metric checks only labels and sample counts, not the observed values.
Claims the duration-seconds histogram check omits status and source labels.
Claims LoggerMiddleware depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running first and would log without plugin identity if reordered.
Claims the metrics middleware now fails the request when the plugin is not in the registry.
The metrics middleware test never asserts that request size is not recorded for CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.
MetricsMiddleware dereferences req (req.Queries, req.Body, req.PluginContext) without a nil-request guard, unlike LoggerMiddleware, so a nil request would panic.
QueryData and CallResource look up the plugin in the registry twice per request.
Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wasted work when backend request logging is disabled because only LoggerMiddleware consumes its context attributes.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: attacker-influenced environment.name and issue title are interpolated unsanitized into PR-comment markdown. WHY: environment comes from event data and title from issue data; backticks/brackets/parentheses break the [**title**](url) template and let an attacker inject markdown/links into bot-posted GitHub/GitLab comments. HOW: escape/sanitize markdown special chars in title and environment before formatting.

WHAT: unauthenticated endpoint loops over unbounded raw_data array running full serializer validation per report with no length cap. WHY: an attacker can POST a huge array to permission_classes=() endpoint causing CPU/memory blowup per request. HOW: enforce a max batch size (e.g. reject >N reports with 422/413).

WHAT: Fallback columnOrder does Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields) which throws when tableData is undefined/null (tableData?.meta evaluates to undefined then .fields access throws) or when meta.fields is undefined. WHY: Crashes table render on empty/loading data instead of rendering empty table, breaking the empty-data story the component explicitly supports. HOW: Use Object.keys(tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}) to safely fallback to empty columns.

issues.descricao: Claims the unauthenticated endpoint iterates an unbounded array of reports, allowing CPU/metric-spam DoS.
Claims BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns Django HttpResponse objects although its Endpoint base expects DRF Response objects.
The assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so requests rejected with 404 are still counted as assemble events, skewing analytics.
BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update() reads validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of 'type', so detector type changes are silently ignored.
Claims get_condition_query_groups indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] and may KeyError for a DCG missing from the precomputed map.
Claims the triggered_actions log now writes the full event payload with user data because event_data was switched to workflow_event_data.
Claims the success path dereferences data.summary without guarding undefined data when the query is disabled or errored.
Claims the column fallback crashes when tableData is defined but meta is missing.
Claims ExploreParams still reads visualize.yAxes after the Visualize class switched to yAxis, producing undefined saved-query params.
Asks to verify that no caller passes Visualize instances instead of BaseVisualize to updateLocationWithAggregateFields.
Claims the number-type test's mock matches query.query instead of substringMatch, so its not-called assertion can never fail.
Claims the attribute key is interpolated into the request path without encodeURIComponent, enabling path confusion.
get_environment_info fetches the recommended event per issue while building the merged-PR comment, an N+1 lookup on the comment path.
The number-type test mock matches on query.query while the hook sends substringMatch, so the mock can never match and the not-called assertion cannot fail.
Claims _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, so PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title raises AttributeError.
Claims the hook now returns undefined attributes before the first fetch instead of {}, which can crash consumers that access keys on the TagCollection.
Claims the default of sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changed from low to off, silently disabling automatic autofix for projects that never set it, unrelated to the replays bulk delete feature.
get_request_data sorts the caller's error_events list in place, mutating its argument as a side effect.
Claims get_environment_info swallows all exceptions with an info log, hiding real failures.
_truncate_title appends an ellipsis after slicing to max_length, so truncated titles exceed ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH by three characters.
